language.script_notes: Street signs commonly read 'Via', 'Piazza', 'Strada', 'Viale', 'Corso', 'Vicolo' — distinct vocabulary from Spanish/French/Portuguese equivalents.

road_furniture.bollard_color: White post with a vertical red rectangle set inside a black diagonal band on the front face; the back face shows a plain white rectangle instead of red — a reliable front/back Italy tell.
road_furniture.bollard_shape: Slim rounded post, distinct diagonal-band reflector pattern from Austria's similar-but-differently-arranged design.
road_furniture.line_paint: White center and edge lines (both 'white outside, white inside' in meta terms) — plain white lines are one of the ways to rule out yellow-line countries like France/Americas.
road_furniture.curb_style: Painted kerbs in towns; cobblestone (sampietrini) streets in historic centers, especially Rome.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: Blue directional arrow road signs; distinctive curve/chevron/roundabout/pedestrian sign designs. Esso, Q8, Eni/Agip, Tamoil and IP are common fuel-station brands.

architecture.roof_style: Low-pitch terracotta tile roofs nationwide; wooden Alpine chalets in the northern mountains.
architecture.roof_material: Red terracotta curved barrel tiles are the standard nationwide roofing material.
architecture.wall_construction: Warm-toned stucco/render walls; baroque stone architecture in Turin and much of the northwest; pastel-painted hill towns; whitewashed cave-dwelling architecture (sassi) in Matera further south.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Ochre, terracotta, pale yellow and cream renders dominate nationwide; pastel-coloured southern hill towns (e.g. Ostuni's whitewashed 'White Town').
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Terracotta-roofed hill towns; Roman-era ruins and cobblestone historic centers; Alpine wooden chalets in the north; whitewashed cave dwellings (sassi) and pastel villages in the south.

nature.vegetation: Cultivated flat farmland (wheat, corn, rice) dominates the Po Valley in the north; Mediterranean evergreen scrub, olive groves, holm oak and cypress trees increasingly dominate moving south; umbrella (stone) pines are a classic central/southern Italy silhouette.
nature.terrain: The Alps form a dramatic northern border; the flat, intensively farmed Po Valley sits beneath them; the Apennine mountains run the length of the peninsula; a long Mediterranean coastline on both sides.
nature.climate_signature: Humid continental with harsh winters in the Po Valley/north; classic sun-bleached Mediterranean climate and light further south.

vehicles.plate_color: White plate with a blue strip on the left carrying the EU stars and 'I' for Italy.
vehicles.plate_format: AA NNN AA (two letters, three digits, two letters).
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Fiat (500, Panda) dominates the small-car segment more than almost anywhere else in Europe — a strong national tell; scooters (Vespa-style) very common in cities.

google_coverage.camera_generation: Mostly Gen 4 across most of the country, giving sharp, high-quality imagery typical of most of modern Western Europe.
google_coverage.coverage_notes: Dense coverage nationwide including most rural and mountain roads.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Terracotta tile roofs, Mediterranean vegetation and climate, similar Latin script and pale/warm-toned architecture
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Italy's bollard has a red-front/white-back diagonal-band design vs. Spain's different reflector style; Italian plates carry only a blue left EU strip while some Spanish plates historically carried yellow rear-only plates; vocabulary differs ('Via' vs 'Calle').

confusion_set.shared_traits: Mediterranean coastline, similar terracotta roofing and cypress/olive vegetation near the shared border
confusion_set.tiebreaker: France's bollards are white with a red-wrapped cap and its road signs use French vocabulary/yellow D-road markers; Italy's roofs run a deeper red and its bollards show the red-diagonal front pattern.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Similar Adriatic coastal architecture, terracotta roofs, cypress trees in Istria specifically
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Croatian/Slovenian plates and script (some Slavic diacritics) differ from Italian; Italy's bollard design and 'Via'/'Piazza' signage are absent across the border.
